conventions.base_color: sRGB hex, authoring space. Ranges are low/high across individuals & species; 'default' is the swatch-render value. Engines convert to linear on import.
conventions.coat: Clearcoat-equivalent (Principled Coat Weight). Represents a literal surface film: saliva, tear film, moisture.
conventions.gltf_export: Per-material note on what survives export: core PBR (base/rough) always; SSS has no core glTF term (KHR_materials_volume is an approximation, most viewers drop it); sheen -> KHR_materials_sheen; coat -> KHR_materials_clearcoat; transmission -> KHR_materials_transmission.
conventions.ior: Physical index of refraction where one is established; else 1.45 (generic organic solid).
conventions.layers: A material may be composite: 'layers' lists sub-records rendered as separate shells/meshes (eye is the only composite in v1).
conventions.metallic: 0 for every material in this set. No living tissue is metallic; do not raise it for wet looks — use coat/specular instead.
conventions.normal: Either {source: 'texture', path} (OpenGL convention, *_nor_gl) or {source: 'procedural', recipe} — procedural entries name the generator the app must implement, so records stay portable before textures exist.
conventions.roughness: 0..1 scalar, glTF metallic-roughness convention (maps to Principled Roughness in Blender). Ranges given where the value legitimately varies (wet/dry, age).
conventions.sheen: weight 0..1 + roughness; the retroreflective fuzz term. Primary tool for fur-adjacent surfaces.
conventions.subsurface: weight 0..1 (Principled Subsurface Weight), radius_rgb = relative chromatic scattering profile (red scatters furthest in all living tissue), scale_mm = mean-free-path scale in millimetres, converted to scene units on import.

materials.gltf_export: Base/rough survive. SSS lost in plain viewers (acceptable: bare-skin areas are small); Blender/MPFB renders keep it.
materials.justification: Living epidermis over a vascular dermis: the red-weighted SSS profile is why ears and muzzles glow against backlight. Measured skin IOR is ~1.38-1.44; dry skin roughness sits mid-range because the stratum corneum is a matte, micro-flaked surface — it only drops toward 0.3 where sebum or moisture films it (that's coat's job, not base roughness). Colour range spans melanin variation across individuals; anthro defaults sit mid-brown so species tinting multiplies cleanly.

normal.recipe: fine pore stipple: voronoi/noise bump, feature size 0.1-0.3 mm, strength 0.15

materials.gltf_export: Base/rough/sheen survive (sheen via KHR_materials_sheen). The fur geometry itself is a separate system (see fur prototype) — this record is only its floor.
intended_parts: all furred body regions — this is the surface the fur cards/shells sit on, and what shows between them
materials.justification: This record deliberately does NOT try to be fur — it is the dark, rough, light-swallowing substrate under a fur system (cards/strands/shells carry the actual coat). Real pelage reads dark at the base because light entering the coat is absorbed before it returns; roughness near 0.9 plus a tinted sheen term reproduces the soft rim halo of a coat without any geometry. SSS is minimal: the coat blocks the light paths that make skin glow. Base colour defaults ~2 stops darker than the intended visible coat colour, since the fur layer multiplies over it.

normal.recipe: fine strand grain: stretched noise along local fur-flow direction, strength 0.2

sheen.note: Sheen colour should be set to the coat's highlight tint (guard-hair colour), not white.

materials.gltf_export: Base/rough/normal survive fully; coat via KHR_materials_clearcoat. This is the most portable material in the set.
materials.justification: The rhinarium is glabrous, heavily keratinised skin kept moist by lateral nasal glands — hence the low roughness and explicit moisture coat over a near-black base. Colour high end (#6b4443) covers the pinker noses of lighter-pigmented individuals and cats; the classic dog/cat nose is at the dark end. Slight SSS (pink-brown) because the tissue is vascular underneath despite the keratin cap.

normal.note: Stand-in grain. Real rhinarium has a polygonal crackle pattern unique per individual; the Poly Haven leather grain (CC0) is the closest on-disk analogue until a dedicated crackle normal is authored.

coat.note: The wet-nose film. Set coat weight 0 for a dry/asleep nose; 0.25 is the healthy awake default.

roughness_map.note: Re-tinted/remapped to the 0.25-0.42 band on import; do not use raw values.

materials.gltf_export: Base/rough survive; SSS (the thing that makes teeth read as teeth) is lost in plain glTF viewers — flagship reason the app renders finals in Blender, not the viewport.
intended_parts: all teeth in the universal arcade (uppers + lowers ride the same record; diet morphs change shape, not material)
materials.justification: Enamel is the most translucent hard tissue in the body — a near-colourless prismatic shell over warm dentine, which is why teeth read ivory rather than white and why the SSS profile here is the warmest (yellow-weighted) in the set. Enamel's measured IOR is ~1.62-1.65, the highest of any material here. Low end of the colour range is the aged/stained state (and the right default for carnivore canines); high end is young/herbivore. Roughness rises with wear — flat herbivore molars sit at the high end.

normal.recipe: very fine vertical perikymata ripples on crowns only, strength 0.05; roots (below gumline) switch to cementum: roughness +0.15, colour toward low end

coat.note: Saliva film in the mouth; set 0 for a dry skull/study render.

materials.gltf_export: Base/rough survive; anisotropy via KHR_materials_anisotropy in supporting viewers, else dropped harmlessly.
intended_parts: horns (same record, scale normal features up)
materials.justification: Claws and horns are compacted keratin lamellae — denser and more translucent than hair, less than enamel; IOR ~1.55 is the keratin standard value. The longitudinal streak normal + anisotropy reproduces the lengthwise fibre structure that makes a claw's highlight run along its curve. Colour spans the real range: near-black horn through amber to pale translucent claw tips (the pale end must keep SSS up or it reads as plastic). Worn/blunt claws take roughness high end; freshly shed/groomed take the low end.

normal.recipe: fine longitudinal growth streaks along the claw axis, strength 0.25

materials.gltf_export: Cornea transmission via KHR_materials_transmission in supporting viewers; iris ball is plain PBR + texture. Worst case (plain viewer): bake cornea highlight into the iris texture's coat and accept a flatter eye.
intended_parts: eyeballs L/R (seated in sockets; iris texture is per-character)
materials.justification: An eyeball is two materials pretending to be one: a pigmented, slightly scattering ball and a transparent refractive shell with a tear film. Splitting them is what produces the deep, wet highlight stack (environment reflection on cornea, softer light inside iris) that a single glossy sphere never achieves. Iris colours above are the natural mammal pigment range — melanin density from blue (none) through green/amber to dark brown; most wild mammals sit amber-to-brown.

base_color.note: TEXTURE-DRIVEN: radial iris texture (procedural generator, see textures note). Iris colour ranges by pigment: amber #b07a2a-#d9a441, gold #c9a227, green #5a7a3a-#7fa050, brown #4a2e18-#6e4a26, blue #5a7f9e-#8fb0c9 (rare, mostly domestic-cat/dog lineages). Sclera (visible in primates/broad-face designs): #ddd6c4 with vein tint at edges; most anthro mammals show almost no sclera — texture should be ~85% iris/pupil coverage.

coat.note: Partial wet coat under the cornea shell; the shell does most of the work.

layers.note: Separate slightly-larger sphere shell. Cornea IOR 1.376 and ~0.5-0.6 mm centre thickness are measured human/mammal values. Pupil dilation is a TEXTURE parameter (pupil radius in the iris texture), not geometry — except slit-pupil species (cats, foxes to a degree), where the pupil shape is baked into the iris texture variant: round / vertical slit / horizontal (herbivore) are three texture families.

normal.recipe: iris radial fibre striations are IN the iris colour texture (baked), not a normal map, at avatar scales

textures_on_disk: anthroforge-v2/materials-lab/textures/iris_amber.png (generated for the swatch render by scripts/gen_iris.py)

materials.gltf_export: Base/rough/coat (KHR clearcoat) survive; SSS loss makes mouths read flat in plain viewers — keep mouths closed in glTF-only contexts or accept it.
materials.justification: Oral mucosa is the most vascular surface on the body — thin epithelium over dense blood supply — so it gets the strongest, reddest SSS in the set and a permanent saliva coat. The default is a healthy canine/feline tongue pink; the low end is the deeper red of a freshly-exercised or darker-pigmented mouth, the high end covers pale/grey-pink variants (and some species' grey tongues should be authored as a desaturated variant, noted not defaulted). Chow-type blue-black tongues are a species variant record, not a range end — the range stays in pink space.

normal.recipe: papillae stipple: dense small bumps (filiform papillae), feature size 0.3-0.8 mm, strength 0.3; gums use a smoother variant (strength 0.12, larger features)

coat.note: Saliva film — this coat is the difference between 'tongue' and 'pink plastic'. Never ship mouth interiors with coat 0.

materials.gltf_export: As a decal/patch material it exports as ordinary PBR; the displacement is the first casualty (bake to normal on export).
intended_parts: scar decals/patches over skin_smooth or skin_furred_base regions
brand/mark variants (deliberate marks use the same record)
materials.justification: Scar is collagen laid down fast and in one direction: fewer blood vessels (paler, less SSS, less red in the profile), no pores or hair follicles (smooth stipple-free normal, aligned streaks instead), and a tighter, slightly shinier surface than surrounding skin — hence roughness BELOW skin_smooth despite being 'damaged' tissue. The derived-colour rule matters more than the exemplar hex: a scar must read as a variant of THIS character's skin, on any species tint. Fresh scars (weeks) break the rule toward red/purple — a 'scar_fresh' variant with SSS 0.4 and saturation restored is the known extension, not in v1.

normal.recipe: aligned fibre streaks along the scar's long axis (collagen laid down in one direction, unlike skin's basket-weave), strength 0.35; no pores

base_color.rule: DERIVED, not absolute: take the host skin colour, raise lightness ~15%, cut saturation ~35%. Absolute exemplar on default skin_smooth: #c39a83.

displacement_mm.note: Hypertrophic default: scars sit PROUD of the surface. Atrophic (sunken) scars use the negative of this range — a per-instance sign flip, not a new record.
